direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale feels both basic and ugly as the whole world just looks cheap and fake, but the dance sequences are still entertaining (which is hard to screw up because it is literally Michael Jackson); The direction on a microscale is pretty artificially fine as they try very hard to force emotional moments, but it does serve its purpose as these interpersonal moments are definitely the better parts of the movie; The storytelling is the most basic, linear storytelling ever because it feels like they are just going through his Wikipedia page from his childhood to after the Thriller era with no depth, making me feel that the Jackson family definitely had a hand in the script; The storytelling is also not good because it feels like a speedrun since it tries to jam too much of his life into just two hours, which is very concerning since this is only part one of two; Tension is built mainly because of the content on the screen and how people react, not because it is actually created well by Fuqua

performance.comments: Really does transform himself into Michael Jackson as he gets his mannerisms down and does get you to empathize with Michael and the struggles he is going through in life; has pretty good chemistry with the rest of the cast; does blended signing with Michael Jackson so gets somewhat of a pass for his singing
Plays the motherly figure well and does support Jackson's performance, but it also feels like she is artificially propped up in many of her scenes
Plays the child Michael very well and really makes you empathize with the abuse he went through as a child, as it shapes him into the man he becomes
Really just feels out of place in this movie, but is somewhat ok and tolerable

Definitely the best actor in this movie as he transforms himself in Joe Jackson and makes himself such a big presence in every scene he is in, inspiring fear not only into the characters but the audience too

cast.comments: There are definitely way too many minor characters in this movie to individually judge, but aggregated, the supporting cast just doesn't move the story forward like they should; the chemistry in the cast is ok, but definitely not the best because of the lack of direction and size

story.comments: The concept is basically a Wikipedia summary of Michael Jackson from his childhood to the end of the Thriller era, but it tries to jam way too much in from this time; The plot structure is very linear, going from Michael Jackson's childhood to the end of the Thriller era; Because this is part one of two, this movie just feels like it is constantly building; This movie would have been so much better if they had just focused on one part of Michael Jackson's life, but because they try to jam so much in, the movie just feels like a speedrun through the first half of Michael Jackson's Wikipedia page; Character writing is incredibly surface-level as they do not tell us anything new about Michael Jackson's life and paint him in a very one-dimensional light, making it very evident that this movie was heavily influenced by the Jackson family; The characterization of Joe Jackson is decent, but it does not tell us anything new

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is fine and does its job to keep you entertained; The humor is still present as they do make jokes that are pretty funny, like the Prince joke; The symbolism is incredibly surface-level and forced as it is so obvious this movie was made by the Jackson family because everything is painted in a one-dimensional light; While you can empathize with Michael's struggle and see why he acts the way he does, this is all just surface-level and forced, especially considering it is just reactionary to what is shown on screen; The foreshadowing is more about building the next movie as it does not really support telling this movie

soundtrack.comments: Amazing considering it is literally just a Michael Jackson Greatest Hits album, what is stopping it from being brilliant is that it is very poorly mixed into the movie

cinematography.comments: Genuinely one of the ugliest movies I have ever seen; The style is so basic yet tries to do so much that it does not know what style it wants to be, making the movie look tacky overall

editing.comments: The editing is so basic yet tries to do so much that it does not know what style it wants to be, making the movie look tacky overall; It is very obvious this movie was edited by the people who did "Bohemian Rhapsody"

sound.comments: The sound really tries to do a lot, but it is still fine for the most part

visual_effects.comments: The visual effects look so fake and cheap that I genuinely wonder where the $200 million went for this movie

production_design.comments: The production design looks so unrealistic and cheap that it makes this feel like a fake movie

makeup.comments: The makeup looks so unrealistic and cheap, except for Colman Domingo's makeup (even though it also looks cheap)

costumes.comments: The costumes are fine for the most part as they try to recreate Michael's iconic looks

review.pacing: Pacing is a general mess as it feels fast because they try to jam in so much of Michael's life, but it also feels slow because the movie is just constantly building
review.climax: The actual climax for this movie is just okay because it simply ends the Thriller era in a very basic way, but I did enjoy the final Bad sequence to segue this movie into the second part showing how Michael is taking more creative control over his life (giving a sneak peek into the next movie)
review.tone: The tone is incredibly Hollywood music biopic because this movie just looks like a fake movie you would see inside the TV of a scene in "Bohemian Rhapsody"
review.final_notes: Part two will really dictate how much the Jackson family intervened with this movie because most of the downfall happens in the second half of his life; If they continue to paint him in a one-dimensional light, it is very obvious they are just trying to use these films as a cash grab while simultaneously trying to protect their family
review.overall: Overall, while the movie is led by two standout performances from Colman Domingo and Jaafar Jackson and plays like a Michael Jackson Greatest Hits album, "Michael" is genuinely one of the ugliest movies I have ever seen because the cinematography and editing are both so basic yet try to do so much, The production design and makeup are so unrealistic that it makes this look like a fake movie, and the visual effects just look so cheap that it makes me wonder where the $200 million budget went; to make matters worse, "Michael" is a linear, surface-level retelling of Michael Jackson's Wikipedia page from his childhood to the end of the Thriller era that tries to jam so much of his life in without providing any depth, making it very evident the Jackson family was involved in making this movie
